newsitem.title: USA: Motorola does not see charges in Q1 like Q4.
newsitem.headline: Motorola does not see charges in Q1 like Q4.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Friday it does not expect to report in the first quarter of 1997 charges similar to those posted in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Late Thursday, the company said its net earnings of $0.39 a share included pretax charges of over $150 million, more than analysts expected.
Last year Motorola reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.72 a share.
"We do not expect similar charges to occur in the first quarter," Ed Gams, head of investor relations, told analysts in a conference call. He did not expand on that outlook.
Motorola had indicated it would take fourth quarter charges of "tens of millions of dollars", analysts said.
"Motorola took a restructuring charge over $150 million, significantly bigger than expected," said Mona Eraiba, an analyst for Gruntal & Co, said in a release.
She said excluding the charge, operating earnings were more than $0.55 a share, topping analysts' estimates.

Motorola said the charges were for restructuring costs and "other unusual charges", including headcount reductions, various asset writedowns and strategic decisions to end certain technology development programs.
The charges were "in comparison with a much smaller charge a year ago," Gams said. A company spokesman said Motorola did not disclose the amount of charges taken in the fourth guarter of 1995.
